title: Washington AI Laws

reading.body:
Washington has enacted one AI-related law, HB2225, which regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring disclosure that they are artificial, recurring notifications, minor protections, and suicide/self-harm response protocols.

The law is narrow in scope. It applies to operators of AI companion chatbots, not to general-purpose models, data centers, or the compute supply chain. Its requirements are behavioral: disclose artificial status repeatedly, restrict sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques for minors, and maintain and publicly disclose protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm.

This matters for AI because Washington's first enacted AI law regulates a consumer application where users may form emotional attachments, not the infrastructure that produces AI. Compliance falls on chatbot operators, not on model training or deployment at scale. The law passed on March 24, 2026.

What is not shown: bills that failed or are pending, enforcement mechanisms, penalties, or how operators implement the required protocols. The law also says nothing about energy, buildings, or compute demand, because it does not address them.

Washington has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Washington

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB2225: Revised for 1st substitute: Regulating artificial intelligence companion chatbots. passed 2026-03-24

    The act regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose that the chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It imposes additional protections for minors, including restrictions on sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It also requires operators to maintain protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and to publicly disclose those protocols.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Washington. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
